_comment: SP-066: the image pick's rubric, read by lib/pick.js (Jev), shaped like scripts/story-rubric.json's axes. One Score question per scored cell and axis; Jev answers a level 0-2, and the axis score is that + 1 (decimals kept, as US-038 keeps them). An axis's optional "check" is added to its question. SP-066 changes SP-064's rubric in two places only (ADR-0033): vivid scores the scene (what the story objects do to each other), not the camera, with the angle exception of C-042; and must-see clarity uses each item's size from the caption, so a small item gets the lowest level. Must-see clarity still checks the items with their adjectives (ADR-0032).

plausible.label: Plausible
levels: the scene makes little sense: no setting clues, or the action happens in an order that doesn't fit the story
the scene makes some sense: a few setting clues, or a mostly sensible order of action
the scene makes sense: clear setting clues such as a floor, a hand or a height, and a sensible order of action

vivid.label: Vivid
vivid.check: Score the scene, not the camera: what the story objects do to each other, from the cell's action line and the sizes of its must-see items. An eye-level, medium shot is the normal view, and an extreme close-up or a strong camera angle adds nothing. An unusual camera angle lowers vivid only when it hides the action; an unusual angle never lowers vivid when the state's angle_case is "view" (the story is about a view) or "one-object" (the story has one main object).
levels: the story objects are small, far away or apart from each other
the story objects are clear, but they don't act on each other as the story says
the story objects are large and act on each other as the story says

clarity.label: Must-see clarity
clarity.check: Check each must-see item with its adjectives: the item must be shown in the state its adjectives give (a bare cob, a nametag that reads "Venice"). The cell's must-see marks say whether the item itself is visible, partly cut or hidden, and give its size (large / medium / small) and place (front / back); they don't check its state. Use each item's size: a small item gets the lowest level.
levels: a must-see item is small, is partly cut off by the edge of the picture, or is not in the state its adjectives give (a cob that isn't bare yet, a nametag that doesn't read "Venice")
every must-see item is shown in full and in the state its adjectives give, and none is small, but some are only medium or unclear
every must-see item is shown in full, in the state its adjectives give, large and clear
